A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RE-PO work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendices A–I are present in both; v4 adds Appendix J. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original alignment evaluations, synthetic-noise experiments, hyperparameter studies, annotator analyses, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: V4 retains original experimental results, including AlpacaEval 2 comparisons, MultiPref evaluations, reliability-estimation experiments, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Table 1, Equations (1)–(7), and Algorithm 1 retain the same preference probabilities, posterior weighting, policy objective, and EMA reliability updates. The new induced-surrogate qualifications explain the existing construction without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UltraFeedback-derived datasets and MultiPref, evaluate on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, and retain the same synthetic-noise scenarios and qualitative task examples.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains standard DPO, IPO, SimPO, CPO, their label-smoothing variants, base models, rDPO, and Hölder-DPO. Tables 3 and 7 retain DPO versus RE-DPO. Corrections from 'HöldeRE-DPO' and 'R-DPO' in prose do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The backbones, single-annotator and MultiPref settings, evaluation metrics, hyperparameter sweeps, synthetic-noise procedures, alternative judge, and controlled runtime protocol remain unchanged. The population-level theorem revision does not revise the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain Table 4's sensitivity study, Figure 2's noise experiments, Figure 3's annotator histograms, Tables 5–6's low-confidence examples, Appendix G's judge comparison, and Appendix H's runtime analysis. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix H and Table 8 retain means and standard deviations over three seeds/runs. Figure 3 retains distribution means and standard deviations across 227 annotators. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The measured results in Tables 2–8 and Figures 2–3 are unchanged. Appendix H corrects the numerical finding that all overheads are within roughly 20%, reporting SimPO overhead of about 32–40% instead. This matches the retained base/RE-PO times of 5383/7557 and 5384.2/7117 seconds.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 and Appendix D replace the finite-dataset update operator and likelihood with population expectations, revise the nondegeneracy assumption, and establish the fixed point through total expectation. This substantially changes the convergence guarantee and removes v3's unjustified equality between a finite empirical average and its population expectation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions qualify arbitrary-loss generality by distinguishing exact likelihood-style equivalence from induced non-likelihood surrogates whose objectives may differ. Reliability recovery is explicitly restricted to the population/full-batch setting under perfect calibration. These materially narrow two central theoretical claims; the up-to-7-point empirical improvement claim remains.

C2.justification: Sections 3–4 clarify the surrogate interpretation and population-versus-finite-sample boundary. Direct likelihood optimization changes from 'intractable' to feasible but coupled and non-convex. Appendix H attributes apparent speedups to system variance instead of seed/padding variance. The existing miscalibration failure limitation remains.

D1.justification: V4 adds a project-page link in the abstract and a reproducibility statement identifying a public code repository. V3's resource appendix provided model and dataset links only. Existing experimental implementation and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 2's substantive positioning remain the same, including connections to Dawid–Skene and Crowd-BT and comparisons with robust losses and data filtering. Citation-style changes and removal of generic novelty wording do not establish changed research positioning.

P1.justification: V4 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, contributions, methodological explanations, proof, and conclusion, and corrects method-name inconsistencies. It adds a reproducibility statement and Appendix J on editorial LLM use, and updates author information. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V4 adopts ICLR title and running-header formatting, restyles headings and table spacing, and reflows existing content. Figure 1 changes 'RPO Loss' to 'Robust Loss'. All three figures and eight tables remain, with the same empirical plots and comparison structures.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses an important validity problem in the central theorem: v3 claims finite-dataset recovery using an invalid empirical-average equality, whereas v4 formulates the argument at population level and uses total expectation. The guarantee becomes narrower but substantially more defensible. Clarifying non-likelihood surrogates and correcting the runtime overstatement further improve consistency between claims and evidence, while retaining the empirical results.
